answer: A submission is accepted only after unrelated peers re-execute it from scratch. If two peers replay the same work, the reward is clawed back and the identity loses standing. The quorum must span unrelated subnetworks, so one operator cannot fill the panel alone. Each clone therefore pays for its own re-execution, and the total cost climbs with every copy; a reward is forged only when the pulse of independent machines agrees, and a summit of identical votes is rejected.
